title: Resilient strange metal at an unconventional quantum critical point in $d=2$
abstract: Properties of the two-dimensional Hubbard model with nearest-neighbor hopping are under scrutiny in cold-atom experiments and diagrammatic quantum Monte Carlo. Given the controlled nature of these approaches, it is timely to make predictions about strange-metal behavior and its relation to quantum-critical properties. Even for interaction strengths below the Mott transition, several peculiarities occur at the quantum critical point separating Fermi liquid and incommensurate spin-density wave order. Here, we predict, using the non-perturbative improved two-particle self-consistent approach, that for correlation lengths ranging from about one to one hundred lattice spacings, Kohn anomalies on the underlying Fermi surface lead to unconventional critical exponents. The temperature dependence of the single-particle self-energy acquires strong momentum dependence along the Fermi surface with no clear evidence of Landau quasiparticles. Nevertheless, we observe strange-metal behavior, namely, resistivity that scales linearly with temperature as $T\rightarrow{0}$. Our work shows that a linear temperature dependence of resistivity arises without a linear-in-temperature self-energy along the Fermi surface, as is often assumed.
summary: This theoretical work predicts that strange metal behavior, characterized by linear temperature dependence of resistivity ($ho \propto T$), persists at an unconventional quantum critical point in the 2D Hubbard model. Using advanced non-perturbative methods, the authors demonstrate this scaling occurs without requiring a simple linear-in-$T$ self-energy correction along the Fermi surface.
main_problem: The study investigates strange metal behavior and its connection to unconventional quantum critical points (QCPs) in two dimensions where standard Fermi liquid theory breaks down.
main_result: The authors predict that resistivity scales linearly with temperature ($ho \propto T$) at the QCP, even when the single-particle self-energy does not exhibit a simple linear-in-$T$ dependence along the Fermi surface.
method: Non-perturbative calculations using an improved two-particle self-consistent approach (TPSC+) are employed to analyze correlation functions and transport properties.
model_or_system: The system modeled is the two-dimensional Hubbard model on a square lattice with nearest-neighbor hopping, focusing on fillings near but above half-filling ($n>1$).
key_observables: Resistivity ($ho$), single-particle self-energy ($\Sigma$), spin susceptibility ($\chi_{sp}$), and charge conductivity ($\sigma_{xx}$).
important_parameters: The analysis is performed near the QCP separating Fermi liquid and incommensurate SDW order, with key parameters including interaction strength $U$ relative to hopping $t$.
main_assumptions: Assumptions include using the Ornstein-Zernicke form for $\chi_{sp}$ and prioritizing gauge invariance when calculating conductivity via current-current correlation functions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate temperature dependencies of spin fluctuation quantities ($\chi_{sp}, \xi^2_{sp}$) showing power laws, confirmation of linear resistivity scaling at low T, and comparisons between theoretical expressions for the f-sum rule.
paper_structure: The paper develops by first establishing the physical context (strange metals near QCPs), then applying advanced many-body techniques (TPSC+) to calculate key susceptibilities and transport coefficients ($\sigma_{xx}$), ensuring gauge invariance throughout the analysis.
why_interesting: While focused on strongly correlated electron systems, the failure of quasiparticle descriptions and the emergence of linear-T resistivity at a QCP are fundamental concepts relevant to non-Fermi liquid physics studied in AMO contexts (e.g., near Feshbach resonances or quantum critical points in ultracold atomic mixtures).

Black dashed lines are power law fits at low temperatures. The resulting exponents are indicated by the in- sets ∼T a. The estimated error on a are ±0.003 for (a), ±0.02 for (b-d) and ±0.01 for (f). (a) Maximum of spin susceptibility at zero frequency. (b) Squared spin correlation length. (c) Squared micro- scopic particle-hole coherence length scale. Obtained from the sec- ond derivative with respect to qx. (d) Landau damping constant. (e) Irreducible spin vertex. (f) Characteristic spin fluctuation frequency obtained from Γ0/ξ2 sp.

FIG. 3. Temperature dependence of resistivity at the SDW QCP (n = 1.1827) for t′ = t′′ = 0, U = 6t. Blue dots are values of resistivity, and the gray line is a linear fit for T ≤0.2t. The inset shows the derivative with respect to temperature.

FIG. 2. (a) Temperature dependence of the imaginary part of the self-energy along the Fermi surface at the QCP (n = 1.1827) for t′ = t′′ = 0, U = 6t. The dashed line is a guide to the eye. The inset in the upper-left corner displays the color code. The full black line is the maximum of the Fermi surface, while the diagonal dashed line is the AFM Brillouin zone. The inset on the lower right shows values at low temperature near the node. This inset has linear axes. (b) Temperature dependence of the single-particle weight along the Fermi surface for the same parameters. Color code in the inset of (a).

FIG. 4. Comparison between the left-hand side (yellow circles) and right-hand side (pink diamonds) of Eq. (16), as a function of temperature, at the QCP (n = 1.1827) for t′ = t′′ = 0, U = 6t. The inset shows the absolute value of the relative difference between the two.

FIG. 5. Zero-frequency spectral weight at the QCP (n = 1.1827) for t′ = t′′ = 0, U = 6t and T = 0.01t. The blue and red diamonds mark 2 points on the Fermi surface related by the incommensurate SDW wavevector Qi = (π, π −ϵ) (in green). The vectors at both points are the renormalized velocities evaluated at their respective points. The inset in the top left corner shows both velocities juxta- posed at the k + Qi point. The inset in the lower right corner shows the Fermi surface (black) and a Fermi surface translated by Qi (red).
